column3: Divided States of America. Devlog one. This is where the game stands after the overnight build, and the tools we built to make it.
A new game starts here. Meridian, Florida, a walled holdout at exit nine on I-95. Morning. Your orders send you to Sheriff Duarte, who has a job about the gators in the canal.
Meridian is lived in now. A market square with stalls, goods on blankets, a fire ring and people working. Burnt shells stand between the rebuilt houses.
You make your survivor point by point. Attributes, a background, traits, and a flaw everyone has to take. The card shows the real body the game draws, in front of your flag.
Controller first. The weapon bar raises fire mode boxes over the gun in your hands. Single, burst, auto. One hand or two. Holster to free your hands.
Pointing a gun is a state. Two armed men draw on you, and nobody fires first. Lower yours, and they lower theirs. A timid man puts his hands up and hands it over.
Survival is the core. Heat and cold, wet clothes, wounds that bleed and go bad, fear and gloom. Each one lights a lamp on the dash, and each one costs you something real.
Vehicles you can walk on. Ride in a pickup's bed, shoot over the side, and get thrown out when it crashes.
The R V is a home. A bed, a stove, a water tank, and a camp you make when you park.
The infected are three kinds of our own. The Greyborn kept a society. Watchers, trappers, an elder at the fire. And they remember you.
The wild is alive by region. Sixteen species, from deer and coyotes in Arizona to gators, hogs and panthers in Florida.
At night a coyote pack stalks the weak, and backs off your light.
And nights are dark now. Truly dark. You see by street lamps, fires and your flashlight. There is a setting, if you need it brighter.
Everything is made of something. Rounds go through wood and stop in block. Doors break. Blood stays on the wall, and dries over the hours.
Death is cloning. You wake in a vat as your last backup. Your body lies where you fell, with everything you carried. You buy a ticket, and ride the bus back to it.
Real rivers from public survey data, carved into the land, with a bridge generated wherever a road crosses one.
Dogs behave like dogs. Feed a stray until it is yours, and it heels, guards, seeks, and fights for you.
Now the tools. The World Forge is one editor for the whole country. Every road, rail, town, exit and base is a row you can see and change, checked by the engine's own rules.
The brush paints the land. Forests, ruins, radiation zones. Paint a stroke, and the running game grows a wood.
The Observer watches a live game. Everyone on the map, the event wire, a card for whoever you click, and replays with heat maps.
The Building Lab lays out real floor plans, proves every room can be reached, and stands the building in the game.
Next, already built on their own branches. The underground. Bunkers, caves, and secret facilities, dark until you get the generator running.
Roadside America. Power lines, gas stations you can siphon, junkyards, farms, and a dam.

column2: NEXT: A BASE IN EVERY STATE
column3: And a military base in every state, at real scale. Sentries, searchlights, drones, and a rail yard.
Two hundred and seventy six checks prove it works. Everything is on main. Open the game, and play.
